No, in SSMS, it's possible to comment and uncomment three SQL queries with the shortcuts which the documentation explains.

Q: How can I solve the red status bar "launching debugger" error? A:

It's because you haven't setup your qml debugger correctly. Set it to default.

Q: Ways to loop through list of dictionaries containing a known pair of keys A:

if you don't display keys then it would be simpler to get .values() instead of .keys() and ...

  • use " ".join() to create string with spaces between values
for i, my_dicc in enumerate( a ):
    print(i, " ".join(my_dicc.values()))
  • use * to unpack values and print() will add spaces between values
for i, my_dicc in enumerate( a ):
    print(i, *my_dicc.values())

This method (with *) should work also when values are not strings but numbers or other elements. Methods with + and with join() will raise error for numbers or other elements.

Q: Why does docker run do nothing when i try to run my app? A:

What are you expecting ? Nothing will happen on the console except the nginx log. You should see something happening if you go to http:ip_of_your_container.

Otherwise, you can just launch your container with this command :
docker container run -d -p 80:80 mywebsite
With this command you'll be able to connect to your nginx at this address http://localhost as you are forwarding all traffic from the port 80 of your container to the port 80 of your host.

Q: R: Number of classes is not equal to 2 A:

Predobject is to be created with 2 inputs to the prediction function:

  1. The list (vector) of predictions (model output, odds or probabilities for each member),
  2. The list (vector) of labels: 0 or 1

as shown in following:

library(ROCR)
data(ROCR.simple)
pred <- prediction( ROCR.simple$predictions, ROCR.simple$labels)

In the case of the question, it is very likely that 2nd parameter (no.miss in above question) is not list of binary info (0,1).

If you get this error, please check your 2nd parameter. I had the same error and providing correct info solved it.

Q: Access File Using http From Local Server A:

Ensure you have python on your computer.(linux)

verify that you have linux by running python -V you should see something like v3.10 Navigate to the directory that you want to share files from run python -m http.server 8000 Go to another device and access this newly created server by typing http://ipaddress:8000 You should see the files
